topic: military mirror-panel countermeasures against AI drone targeting
title: The Weird Reason Militaries Are Bolting Mirrors to War Vehicles
description: Why some armored vehicles are getting wrapped in mirror panels -- and how it messes with AI-powered targeting systems. AI-narrated commentary, original script.

hook_candidates.text: Militaries just found the cheapest way to beat an AI-guided drone: a mirror.
What if the smartest AI vision system in the world could be tricked by something in your bathroom?
Everyone assumes beating AI drone targeting takes more AI. Turns out it takes glass.
AI can spot a tank from a mile away -- until you wrap it in mirrors.

beats.text: Militaries just found the cheapest way to beat an AI-guided drone: a mirror.
beats.broll_query: military vehicle covered in mirror panels

beats.text: AI vision systems are trained to recognize the sharp edges and shapes of vehicles -- tanks, trucks, jeeps.
beats.broll_query: AI computer vision object detection military vehicle

beats.text: So troops started bolting angled mirror panels onto their vehicles, scattering and warping the light bouncing back.
beats.broll_query: reflective mirror panels on truck close up

beats.text: To a human eye it barely looks camouflaged. To a drone's AI, the reflections break the outline it's trained to lock onto.
beats.broll_query: drone camera view targeting confusion glare

beats.text: It's a strange twist -- the more advanced the targeting AI gets, the more it can be fooled by something as old as a mirror.
If you think low-tech beats high-tech more often than we admit, drop an example in the comments.
